tables.title: Character values
tables.description: These values belong to the current-character word at array index 1 (byte offset +0x04). The word is an ID, not a character-unlock bitmask.

tables.title: Runtime mirror fields
tables.description: The declaration is a 32-bit-word array. Multiply the array index by four to obtain a byte offset; the symbol itself is the storage base.
rows: Activation marker: the native save-start path writes 1 after copying the 0x30-byte runtime block. Other values are not assigned an enum meaning here.
Current character ID; see Character values above. This word also resides at native address 0x8015C5DC.
Current health in half-heart units. Also exported as [D_8015C5E4](./D_8015C5E4.md); the unsigned array declaration does not change the underlying health field.
Character-change/dirty marker: the character-switch path writes 1. The complete reset protocol is not established here.

tables.title: System structure fields
tables.description: Dereference this pointer once, then use these offsets from the full system structure base (0x8008CCC0 in the US executable). D_800BCCC0_BD8C0 is an interior alias 0x30000 bytes farther into the same structure.
rows: Game-loop timing/control byte; the system-step setter writes 2.
Game-loop/frame counter; a running numeric counter, not a state ID.
Main system step. Known entries are listed below.
Main-step completion/substate byte; the step setter clears it to 0.
Native start-sequence gate. Zero is the cleared value used for normal gameplay; nonzero values must retain their native sequence meaning.
Player control mask (D_800C7AE0). Either low bit in mask 0x03 suspends the native late player collision handlers.
Scripted player input state (D_800C7AE3). The native move-toward and input-playback paths set it while supplying scripted input.
Destination-transition marker; the warp destination helper writes 1.
Seventh argument of the warp destination helper; individual values are not yet interpreted.
Eighth argument of the warp destination helper; individual values are not yet interpreted.
Destination room/stage ID. Use the room table on D_800C7AB2.

tables.title: Known main-system steps
tables.description: These are selected established values of the byte at full-system offset +0x3ADD4. A step change depends on initialized native callbacks and related state; this is not a complete state-machine enum.

tables.title: Graphics-bank layout
tables.description: Offsets are relative to one bank, beginning at full system base + bank_index × 0x1D6D8. There are two banks; these fixed arrays are distinct from CPU task and display-record storage.
rows: Additional native workspace; individual fields are not interpreted here.
Additional native workspace; individual fields are not interpreted here.
Final native workspace, ending at bank offset 0x1D6D8.

tables.title: Interior-alias field offsets
tables.description: This exported byte array begins at full-system offset +0x30000. Use the alias-relative offset in this table when indexing D_800BCCC0_BD8C0 directly; adding a full-pointer offset to this alias addresses the wrong memory.
rows: Game-loop timing/control byte; the system-step setter writes 2.
Game-loop/frame counter; a running numeric counter, not a state ID.
Main-step completion/substate byte; the step setter clears it to 0.
Native start-sequence gate. Zero is the cleared value used for normal gameplay; nonzero values must retain their native sequence meaning.
Destination-transition marker; the warp destination helper writes 1.
Seventh argument of the warp destination helper; individual values are not yet interpreted.
Eighth argument of the warp destination helper; individual values are not yet interpreted.
Destination room/stage ID. Use the room table on D_800C7AB2.

tables.title: Health units
tables.description: The native field is a signed 32-bit health count measured in half-hearts. These rows show the unit conversion; they are numeric quantities rather than distinct state-enum entries. Native new-save health is ten half-hearts and is copied into this runtime word during save activation.
rows: Five hearts; native new-save current health after activation.

tables.title: Current health and Tsurami gate
tables.description: This native current-health word is located at save-base offset -0x24; see the [save field layout](./D_8015C608_15D208.md#save-field-layout). Tsurami uses the word as a zero/nonzero gate before its private post-update body, rather than testing whether health is positive.
rows: Current health is zero; skip the gated Tsurami private post-update body.
Current health is nonzero; the gate allows the private post-update body. The native test is != 0, not > 0, and other callback conditions still apply.

tables.title: Actor instance fields
tables.description: Offsets are relative to the actor instance pointed to by this variable, not to the pointer storage. A null definition pointer terminates the instance list during native actor-manager traversal.
rows: Spawn position X, Y and Z.
Spawn rotation: pitch, yaw and roll.
Actor definition record; zero terminates the native instance list.
Spawn-state byte. A full raw-value interpretation is not established.

tables.title: Actor definition fields
tables.description: Offsets are relative to the definition record pointed to by the variable. Parameters and the three data words are actor-specific.
rows: Actor ID: indexes the entry-callback and actor metadata tables.
Three actor data words copied to task offsets +0xD0, +0xD4 and +0xD8 by the native initializer.

tables.title: Known actor IDs
tables.description: Selected actor IDs with established descriptive names. Names distinguish actor types and variants; they do not define the parameters or behavior of every instance.

tables.title: Resident resource entry fields
tables.description: The registry has 48 entries. Each N64 record occupies 8 bytes. Scan only until the first entry whose file ID is zero; its data pointer records the next free resident-arena position.
rows: File ID. Zero terminates the occupied entries.
Loaded data base for a nonzero file ID; next free arena position for the first zero-file-ID entry.

tables.title: Recycling-owner values
tables.description: A non-null value must identify a valid native owner. Nullness alone does not establish ownership, record availability, or pointer lifetime.
rows: No optional recycling owner; use the normal kind-2 allocation path.
The single-allocation helper first asks this owner to release one record.

tables.title: Initial pool capacities
tables.description: These are the first eight 16-bit entries in the verified US image. The array index is the pool kind, while the stored value is a capacity. Initialization can change capacities. Only kind 2 has an established record-type name here.
rows: Pool capacity; the record-type name is not established.
Pool capacity; the record-type name is not established.
Pool capacity; the record-type name is not established.
Pool capacity; the record-type name is not established.
Pool capacity; the record-type name is not established.
Pool capacity; the record-type name is not established.
Pool capacity; the record-type name is not established.

tables.title: Counter representation
tables.description: Single kind-2 allocation-request telemetry. It increments before capacity checks, so requests can be counted even when allocation fails.
rows: Numeric counter, not an enum or bitmask. The broader reset interval is not established.

tables.title: Counter representation
tables.description: Peak value maintained by the single kind-2 allocation path; it is telemetry rather than the current active record count.
rows: Numeric counter, not an enum or bitmask. The broader reset interval is not established.

tables.title: Known pool-count index
tables.description: The array contains signed 16-bit active-allocation counts. Pool-kind indices must not be confused with the actor-owner categories in D_802297D6_5E4CA6.
rows: Active model/display records. This element is also exported as D_8016DADC_16E6DC.

tables.title: Active model/display count
tables.description: This signed 16-bit value aliases D_8016DAD8_16E6D8[2]. Compare it to the kind-2 capacity; it is not a flag or a telemetry request count.
rows: No active kind-2 records according to the native active-allocation counter.
That many kind-2 records are active.
Not a valid ordinary active count; no special negative state is established.

tables.title: Current task fields
tables.description: Offsets are relative to the current task pointer. The first callback/object fields belong to the shared task prefix. Actor-extension fields below apply to ordinary actor tasks; the playable-player task has a different +0x5C meaning.
rows: Ordinary actor ID. Do not use this interpretation for the player task.
Health field for the actor types that use this layout.

tables.title: Known task masks
tables.description: These masks belong to fields of the pointed-to task. They are not flags stored in D_8016DAB4_16E6B4 itself.
rows: Callback is disabled. Preserve the native callback representation when changing this bit.

tables.title: Player task fields
tables.description: Dereference the variable to obtain the player task. In this task type, +0x5C is a pointer to player work, rather than the ordinary actor-ID field.
rows: Contact flags: bit 0x01 accepts ordinary incoming hits, 0x02 enables outgoing attack scans, and 0x04 selects the native special incoming-hit filter.
Victim task hit by this task during the native scan; nonzero stops further victim scanning.
Incoming attacker task. Native collision-dependent callbacks consume this hit record.
Unscaled body radius copied from D_801FC660_5B8570 for the selected character. Native body contacts apply object scale X.
Unscaled body height copied from D_801FC668_5B8578 for the selected character. Native body contacts apply object scale Y.
One-based sphere index recorded by an incoming native contact. This is not a health-damage amount.
Active outgoing attack descriptor. Zero disables attack volumes; 0xFFFFFFFF selects the fixed sphere fields.
Native outgoing attack kind used by victim filters and damage handling; separate from the sphere index.
Player damage invulnerability countdown. While nonzero, the updater applies D_800C7A78 parity to render-object +0x64; expiry restores visible rendering and ordinary incoming contact.

tables.title: Known player action values
tables.description: These are selected values of the action byte at player task +0xCC. Action semantics can depend on the selected character; this is not a complete native action list.

tables.title: Player work fields
tables.description: First read the pointer at task +0x5C, then apply these work-relative offsets. These fields are not located directly in the task.
rows: Character-change marker; the native character setter writes 1.
Goemon Sudden Impact marker; the appearance reader recognizes exactly 1 as active. Other values are not established active states.
Ebisumaru small-form marker: nonzero spans the shrink/small/grow interval; the native character-change path clears it to zero.

tables.title: Player render-object fields
tables.description: Offsets are relative to the pointed-to render object. Position, scale and animation frame are continuous values. Segment slots pair resource identifiers with resident data bases.
rows: Render-object mode; value 2 selects the native clothed-character object mode. Other modes are not enumerated here.
Auxiliary character-resource data bases selected by descriptor values 3 and 4.
Render flags: bit 0x01 suppresses kind-2 model drawing. Native hurt recovery alternates this bit by D_800C7A78 parity; collision and model/scale data remain intact.

Native clipping/visibility state. Drawing is suppressed only for negative values; both 0 and positive values are accepted. The kind-2 reset template initializes this byte to 1, while the generic display constructor clears it to 0.

tables.title: Character action-table pointers
tables.description: The outer array is indexed by character ID. The stored values below are the native US overlay addresses of each character’s action-record table; they are meaningful only while that overlay is resident.

tables.title: Action metadata record
tables.description: Select a character table, then add action_id × 0x1C. The record is 28 bytes long. Only interpreted fields are listed; gaps must not be assumed unused.
rows: Animation step in hundredths: divide by 100.0 to obtain the frame increment.
Action model-data start address, using the 0x07 segment tag.
Action model-data end address. Zero instructs the native action-range loader to use the end of the selected action file.
Initial auxiliary row selected for the second auxiliary channel.

tables.title: Auxiliary resource rows
tables.description: Each auxiliary row occupies 8 bytes. These are nested records reached through action metadata +0x18.
rows: Resource ID. Zero means no resource bind; 0xFF is the timed-sequence loop marker.
Animation-frame threshold component. Cursor advancement also depends on the accumulated threshold and frame-reset conditions; zero is not a universal stop flag.

tables.title: Initial auxiliary descriptors
tables.description: The established portion contains two byte pairs. The second byte selects an object base slot using +0x38 + selector × 8. The first byte of each pair is preserved as uninterpreted data.

tables.title: Timed auxiliary descriptors
tables.description: The array stores 16-bit descriptors. The low byte selects the object base slot using +0x38 + selector × 8; the meaning of the upper byte is not established.
rows: Object base slot +0x50; upper byte is zero.
Object base slot +0x58; upper byte is zero.

tables.title: Broad character resource IDs
tables.description: The array index is a character ID (0–3). The stored 16-bit value is a native file ID, not an address or a character ID. These are the initial US overlay values.

tables.title: Action-model resource IDs
tables.description: The array index is a character ID (0–3). The stored 16-bit value is a native file ID, not an address or a character ID. These are the initial US overlay values.

tables.title: Known appearance replacement tables
tables.description: These are indices of a pointer array, not appearance-flag bits or character IDs. The pointed-to replacement data is overlay resident.
rows: Replace Goemon’s normal hair display pointers with Sudden Impact variants.
Reverse the substitution and restore Goemon’s normal hair display pointers.

tables.title: Opaque sound-state storage
tables.description: No individual field, byte value, or complete structure size has been established for this buffer. It does not have a known value enum.
rows: Pass the base address unchanged to the native scene sound helper; individual bytes are not documented controls.

tables.title: Camera-vector components
tables.description: This is direct Vec3f storage, not a pointer variable. Values are continuous single-precision coordinates, not room or camera-mode IDs.

tables.title: Camera-radius representation
tables.description: This symbol stores a continuous single-precision radius value. No fixed set of numeric presets or universal safe range is established.
rows: Camera radius/distance quantity. Read it as a float; the underlying 32-bit bit pattern is not an integer radius.

tables.title: Impact battle-state fields
tables.description: These offsets are relative to the live Impact battle-state pointer. The state is meaningful only during the corresponding battle mode.
rows: Boss health. The battle helper tests whether it is greater than zero.
Combat pause gate: zero means not paused by this gate; nonzero means paused.

tables.title: Selected actor entry addresses
tables.description: The array index is an actor ID. These are stored entry addresses from the US actor table; 0x08000000-region addresses belong to dynamically loaded actor code and require the matching resident overlay. See [`D_8015CDE0`](./D_8015CDE0.md#known-actor-ids) for more actor IDs.

tables.title: Actor metadata lookup layout
tables.description: The symbol covers two packed tables with different element widths. Use an actor ID, not a pool-kind index.
rows: Native actor-owner category passed to func_80219CA0_5D5170.

tables.title: Selected actor metadata values
tables.description: These stored values are read from the verified US table. Model IDs and owner categories are different numeric domains from the actor ID used to index the table.

tables.title: Owner category values
tables.description: Native categories select owner pointers and sometimes an additional per-category cap. The function first applies its overall actor-cap checks. Owner-pointer locations below contain pointers; the addresses are not owner tasks themselves. Category labels beyond this routing behavior are not established.
rows: Owner pointer stored at `0x8015CCD4`. Applies the category cap stored at `0x8015CCE8`.
Owner pointer stored at `0x8015CCBC`. Applies the category cap stored at `0x8015CCE0`.
Owner pointer stored at `0x8015CCD0`. Applies the category cap stored at `0x8015CCF0`.
Owner pointer stored at `0x8015CCD0`. Applies the category cap stored at `0x8015CCE4`.
Owner pointer stored at `0x8015CCD4`. Applies the category cap stored at `0x8015CCEC`.

tables.title: Initial stage scale
tables.description: This is a continuous IEEE-754 single-precision scale, not an enum. The value below is the initial scalar in the verified US stage overlay; running game state can change writable data.
rows: Uniform X/Y/Z scale passed by the native actor manager when creating ordinary actor model objects.
